<explanation>
Based on our analysis of Maigret’s file structure and README, here’s how you can draw an accurate, detailed architecture diagram tailored to this OSINT investigation tool:

1. Project Type & Purpose:
   • Maigret is an OSINT tool for collecting online profiles and activity by username – a fork of Sherlock. It checks over 3000 sites and supports various report formats (HTML, PDF, XMind), with both command-line and web interface functionality.
   • The tool emphasizes modular design for scalable searching, report generation, and integration with external websites.

2. Main Components:
   a. Core Engine:
      – Located primarily within the "maigret" directory.
      – Contains the central logic (maigret/maigret.py) for the search operations, interacting with modules like:
         • sites.py: defines supported sites and parsing logic.
         • result.py: processes and structures search results.
         • checking.py, executors.py, submit.py: manage task execution and data retrieval.
         • notify.py & report.py: handle communications and output generation.
      – Utilities in "maigret/utils.py" and "maigret/permutator.py" help enable advanced search and permutations.
      – Resource configuration (data.json, settings.json, report and PDF templates) is housed under "maigret/resources".

   b. Interfaces:
      • Command-Line Interface (CLI):
         – Houses the entry point (“maigret/__main__.py”) to trigger searches.
         – Provides various options to output reports in different formats.
      • Web Interface:
         – Found in the "maigret/web" subdirectory.
         – Contains the web application (app.py) along with a set of HTML templates (in the templates folder) and supporting static files.
         – Allows users to launch Maigret with the “--web” flag, view interactive result graphs, and download reports.
   
   c. Packaging, Distribution & Configuration:
      – Top-level files such as Dockerfile, pyproject.toml, and Installer.bat indicate multiple deployment options: pip installation, Docker, and standalone EXEs.
      – The "pyinstaller" folder contains standalone packaging information.
      – The presence of a Makefile and various README/documentation files shows that build automation and user/developer guidance are integral.

   d. Additional Components:
      • Testing:
         – The “tests” directory covers unit tests and integration tests for nearly every module.
      • Documentation:
         – The “docs” folder and README provide extensive usage and development guidelines.
      • Utilities Scripts:
         – In the "utils" folder and helper scripts like "wizard.py" for additional functionalities or administrative tasks.
   
3. Relationships & Data Flow:
   – Begin with the user input (via CLI or Web UI):
      • For CLI, the input is processed in the main entry file which calls into the core search engine.
      • For the web interface, HTTP requests are handled in maitre/web/app.py, triggering the same backend logic used in CLI.
   – The Core Engine then:
      • Reads configuration/resources.
      • Iterates through supported sites (via sites.py) and executes search queries.
      • Processes and structures the results.
      • Sends data to the reporting modules (report.py) to generate outputs (HTML, PDF, XMind).
   – Reporting outputs are either saved locally or served through the web interface.
   – Utility modules and external scripts play a supportive role through data updates, tag handling, or site imports from "utils/*".
   – External interactions (network requests to websites, possibly through HTTP client libraries) are a key element, and retries or parsing logic (errors, checking modules) manage robustness.
   
4. Architectural Patterns & Design Principles:
   • Modular design: Separation between the core logic, interfaces, and utilities.
   • Layered architecture: The presentation layer (CLI & Web) is decoupled from the business (search and report generation) and data/resource layers.
   • Plug-in extensibility: New sites can be added easily by updating configuration files (data.json) and extending parsing logic.
   • Testing & Continuous Integration: A robust suite of tests (in tests/) supports maintainability.
   
5. Diagram Guidelines:
   – Create distinct blocks for each component:
      • Use separate boxes for the CLI Interface, Web Interface, Core Logic, Reporting Engine, Data/Configuration Resources, and Utilities.
   – Draw directional arrows to depict:
      • Data flow from user interfaces to the core engine.
      • Communication from the core engine to external websites (depicted, for example, as a generic “External Services” box).
      • Flow from the core engine to the reporting modules.
      • Dependencies from utilities and configuration resources into the core engine.
   – Label each arrow to clarify actions (e.g., “User Request”, “Search Query”, “Report Generation”).
   – Employ color coding or shape variations:
      • Use one color/shapes for presentation layers (CLI and Web), another for backend modules, and a third for configuration/data resources.
   – Include peripheral components:
      • Draw smaller nodes or annotations for testing, packaging (Docker, PyInstaller), and deployment.
      • Optionally, indicate that the OSINT process interacts with external sites, showing a clear path from “Core Engine” outwards.
   
6. Tailoring the Diagram to Maigret:
   – Emphasize the dual-interface model, making sure both CLI and web interfaces connect to a single core engine.
   – Highlight the modularity in the core logic, showing sub-modules like site parsing logic, reporting, and data configuration.
   – Mark extensions and utilities (the “utils” folder, scripts like wizard.py) as auxiliary but important enhancement components.
   – Include deployment and packaging mechanisms (Dockerfile, standalone executables) in a separate “Deployment & Distribution” section.
   
By structuring the diagram in this manner—with clear labels, arrows for data flow, differentiated colors, and detailed components—you will have a comprehensive representation of the Maigret architecture. This will help in understanding how the system integrates its core OSINT search capabilities with multiple interfaces and deployment options, while ensuring that every key component is clearly mapped and its interdependencies are well represented.
</explanation>
